sources.relevant_locator: Proposition 7; journal p.300; downloaded author manuscript p.27
sources.source_attribution: Proposition is explicitly attributed there to A. Chademan, Bounded algebraic critical values (1996); that original 1996 text was not read.
sources.theorem_paraphrase: A complex polynomial with critical-value set exactly {0} is A(z-z0)^n.
complete_hypothesis_map: A target polynomial cannot have degree one.
If a is nonzero, P-a has n distinct roots, contradicting the degree of P prime-a. Thus a=0.
P prime=0 implies P=0, so all critical values are zero; degree at least two makes this set nonempty.
P prime-b has n-1 distinct roots; if k<n, P kth derivative-b has smaller degree and cannot vanish at all of them; k>n also fails.
For k=n the constant derivative equals b iff A=b/n!.
sources.implication_status: complete polynomial classification as a short corollary of a prior explicit theorem plus degree counts
